Boot a stick

The feedback we hear most is "keep it simple". So here is the whole setup for local LLMs on a Ryzen AI MAX+ 395 (Strix Halo) machine:

  1. Download the 1bit OS image from the releases page.
  2. Write it to a USB stick of 8 GB or more.
  3. Boot the machine from the stick. Secure Boot stays on; the image is signed.
  4. Lemonade comes up with its catalog and its web UI. Pick a model and talk to it.

If you like it, one command from the live session installs the 1bit appliance to the disk: 1bit-install <disk> --yes. It refuses to write anything until it has printed the disk it is about to use and waited, so a typo cannot cost you a drive. Reboot without the stick and the machine is the same appliance, now permanent.

What is on the stick#

A Lemonade Server with the 1bit engine embedded as its onebit backend. Lemonade is the server you talk to: its model catalog, its downloads, its router, its UI, its OpenAI-compatible API. For the models it hands to the engine, the Radeon 8060S iGPU runs them through HRX with our own HIP kernels and the XDNA 2 NPU runs them through our own NPU runtime. Nothing to configure, nothing to compile, no driver to install: the kernel on the stick is ours, built and signed for this hardware.

The same engine is also a package for a Lemonade you already run on Ubuntu, from the same releases page (Lemonade).

Where it stands#

The current candidate image passes 17 of 17 checks on the board, booted from the stick with Secure Boot on. The release itself goes out when every item on the checklist is done; the checklist and the candidate's pins are public (Releases). The models the image is checked against, with the number each one measured on this hardware, are one page (Models measured).

Sources: README, Releases, os/v2/README.md.
